item.title: Agent swarms are the next scaling frontier for AI. For years, we’ve scaled intelligence by training larger models and giving them more time to think. But there’s another dimension: running many agents in parallel, exploring different approaches, challenging each other, and working together on solut...
item.description:
作者：Amjad Masad 账号：@amasad 简介：ceo @replit. civilizationist
Agent swarms are the next scaling frontier for AI.
For years, we’ve scaled intelligence by training larger models and giving them more time to think. But there’s another dimension: running many agents in parallel, exploring different approaches, challenging each other, and working together on solutions that no single agent could easily discover.
OpenAI has already demonstrated the potential of this approach with breakthroughs in mathematics.
Until now, experimenting with agent swarms yourself required building complicated orchestration infrastructure.
Starting today on Replit, spinning up a swarm of agents is just one prompt away.
Excited to see what people discover when we make collective machine intelligence programmable by anyone.

item.title: devin bots are multi-agent teams done right: - always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI) - own outcomes not tasks (but can collab w others) - manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself) - available everywhere (call text slack whatever hello @interaction) - consistent reporting thru interactive ar...
item.description:
作者：Swyx 账号：@swyx 简介：achieve ambition with intentionality, intensity, integrity & insanity.
affiliations: - @smol_ai - @cognition - @temporalio - @aidotengineer - @latentspacepod
devin bots are multi-agent teams done right: - always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI) - own outcomes not tasks (but can collab w others) - manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself) - available everywhere (call text slack whatever hello @interaction) - consistent reporting thru interactive artifacts aka devinapps not long chats (HTML is all you need™ @trq212)
this is the preview that @walden_yan gave at AIE. i've been trialing them for a week and i've been able to hand over my AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin automation, and video editing work (also simultaneously moving from local agent worktree hell to cloud because ofc this is all cloud based thank god)
hyped concepts this replaces: - /goal - "ultracode" / "ultra mode" - "loop engineering" - "agent to agent" - "agent swarms" - AI employees (see below)
my main aha moment is that you don't want "AI Employees", we do not have agi yet and you will just fail if you overpromise/overexpect. what you want is the "just" the next level of abstraction above single tasks, and the overwhelming consensus I've had talking to everyone at the frontier of agents (yes incl cog competitors) is agent managers that own outcomes.
incidentally, as an employer of humans it's also how i distinguish between someone who "has agency" (owns a problem area, finds issues and researches/brings solutions not problems) and who doesn't (only does precisely what i asked, not proactive, doesn't come up with suggestions i didn't think about). guess which one i value more lol.
if youre a startup, reminder that Devin for Startups offers 65k in credits. apply via clanker

item.description:
作者：Josh Woodward 账号：@joshwoodward 简介：VP, @Google @GoogleLabs @GeminiApp @GoogleAIStudio
Gemini can now do your tasks free of charge in six countries! We’ve built it for anyone who has tasks piling up during all the classes, meetings, and school drop-offs that fill the day. Our goal is for Gemini to get the job done and save you time and money along the way.
3 major updates:
1) Running on our new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, Gemini can get stuff done at no cost for hundreds of millions of people across the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India.
2) Many highly requested features are rolling out now, starting in the US: * Call local businesses (via Google Duplex) * Pay and check out (via Google Pay) * Text Gemini on Android or iOS (via RCS) * Forward emails to Gemini (via Gmail) * Sign into sites without sharing passwords outside Google (via Google Password Manager)
3) We’ve also landed our biggest update yet for the Gemini <> Google Workspace integration. The tools trigger more reliably, and you can do much more without ever leaving Gemini. Draft or send emails. Create and edit Docs or Sheets. Add multiple Calendar events at once.
Ready to hand off your next task? We can’t wait to see what Gemini crosses off your list first.

item.title: Building Visual Intelligence — Andreas Blattmann & Dustin Podell, Black Forest Labs
item.description:
播客：Latent Space
Happy to bring to you our episode with Black Forest Labs.
Our guests today are Andreas Blattmann, he also goes by Andi, who is co-inventor of latent diffusion, the technique that eventually got scaled up by Stable Diffusion and Stability AI, and they eventually split with a bunch of, uh, the core Stability AI image gen folks to form Black Forest Labs.
And Dustin Podell, who I also met with Anj, uh, at one of the stories that we tell, and, uh, who worked his way up from just being a regular engineer, a freelance, like, web developer person, into a model and research lead at Stability AI, and now, uh, Black Forest Labs, creator of SDXL, Control LoRA, post-training lead on SD3, Flux Ultra, Flux.1, and Flux Context.
And we go into all of these details. Um, as you may know, sometimes we're very honored to have an extended history with some of our guests, and this is one of them.
You might have heard in our Anj Mittal episode where we talked about introducing each other at one of the NeurIPS's [smacks lips] and meeting Black Forest Labs for the first time.
And, uh, this was right after Stable Diffusion.
But what you may not have heard, and we only tell this story in this episode, is how latent space itself was started because of Stable Diffusion, directly, uh, crediting the launch for me basically quitting my job to go all in on AI based on what we saw.
And today's guest, Dustin, also [chuckles] had that experience, and so did Vibhu.
And so we have a very, very strong tie with the team that basically led up to Black Forest Labs, and now we're also interested in what's next for them.
Like, they have created some of the best open and closed weights models for image generation and video generation.
I think especially Flux Context, if you're not aware of image editing models, I do think that this is in the ex-in the limit one of the things to fully replace Canva and, um, and Photoshop and a bunch of other workflows and editors that you might use in a normal creative workflow.
It is not going to replace the top end of the market. But for regular, normal, everyday edits, why would you not want anything else other than to query a model and ask it to do, uh, image editing for you?
Uh, we do this obviously with this kind of video editing. It's all Clanker done, and I do review it, and they're also moving into robotics.
And so this ties in with a miniseries of model labs that have been pursuing this direction, building world models from image gen, like with Runway, uh, as well as, um, video models and now robotics models.
And so I think a lot of things rhyme in a lot of our recent episodes, like even the artificial analysis episode that we're gonna release soon, they are also going into robotics, and, like, it seems pretty s- obvious that when you see a whole bunch of smart people who are at the frontier all leaning one direction, that you're probably six to 12 months out from some kind of really big breakthrough.
This has been a consistent theme over my last four years of podcasting. It's not gonna change now. So look out for it. Um, that's the [chuckles] most obvious call-out I can make.
But there's also a lot of interesting lore for people interested in the general diffusion space. Uh, we're gonna d- do a little bit more over time.
I, I'm thinking about an AI- AIE LA, where we talk about the generative media field and the creative arts and how, uh, that complicated relationship is evolving, um, and I think maturing, to be honest.
And finally, for those longtime listeners, uh, we are starting to open up to advertisers, people that we really admire and respect and wanna showcase what they're working on.
Um, the first one was with Supabase, which I think a lot of you enjoyed, and the second one today is brought to you by Deepgram, and you'll hear more from us at the midpoint of the episode.
[upbeat music] You should be showing a robot an action one time, and then it should be able to do this, and this would be truly a superhuman intelligence like- At Stability that we couldn't essentially leverage the value of what the models could be as well as the mistakes of not being able to actually capture the value of the models themselves.
We raised all in all four hundred and fifty million, uh- Oh my God... dollars of funding so far. Yeah. Currently, the last, uh, that was published in, uh, December was one hundred million in revenue.
BFL was not founded to be an image generation lab. Video modeling is actually the central means to understanding how our world basically works. It was maybe, like, six hours of training, four hours of training.
It, it was, it was a very, very short training run, and all of a sudden, like, I saw what felt like a clear generality coming out of it, 'cause it was [upbeat music] Okay. Finally, our BFL pod.
Welcome, guys, Andreas and Dustin. [chuckles] Great to be here. Thank you so much. Thank you. Yeah, definitely thank you for having us. I know we've chatted about doing this for a long time. Yes.
So we've had Anj on a couple times, and that's where I met you, at Vienna, I think one of the ICMLs or- Was this, like, one of the, like, was, was the, like- The-... rooftop, uh, event, or, or what was it?
There was a year where there were two Viennas back to back. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. That was first ICLR, and then it was ICML. Yeah, yeah. I don't know how they do this thing. [laughs] Yeah.
Anyway, anyway, uh, and, and at the time you guys had-- were, like, just about to, uh, launch BFL. Like, we had a dinner and, like, you were like, oh, and thinking about what's next after Stability and, uh, all that.
So, uh, anyway, congrats. How do you like, guys, like to introduce yourself? Maybe we'll sort of get a crisp, uh, self-intro up front. So I'm Andi. I'm a co-founder of Black Forest Labs.
Been developing diffusion models for, oh, wow, I think seven years now. Uh, met Robin and Patric way, way back in the day. I think it's, yeah, seven years now since we met at Hei- in Heidelberg.
Uh, I'm from Germany o- uh, originally. And there we started looking into, yeah, just diffusion modeling for images.
Uh, we were all having a kind of a physics background, um, in some sense, and this, this paradigm of just, like, mapping this general physical phenomena of diffusion to machine learning and generative modeling had a, a kind of a, a philosophical kind of beauty to us.
That's why we got into this. And then, yeah, developed a lot of the, I guess, fundamental algorithms that are powering diffusion models today, or image generation, video generation, and also action prediction today.
I guess we'll talk about this later We'll talk about it. But, um- Yeah, uh, this of, of a kind related to... It's not immediately obvious to people, image generation to action prediction. Yeah.
But we can talk about that. Uh, and then one, one thing I did wanna comment is a lot of people don't know the relationship. Black Forest is a forest in Germany? It's a mountain range, actually. Ah.
